origin_issue.title: [BACKEND] [STORY] Execution: Apply Role-Based Visibility in Execution UI

clarification_issue.title: [CLARIFICATION] Origin #155: [BACKEND] [STORY] Execution: Apply Role-Based Visibility in Execution UI

clarifications_resolved.question: What is the authoritative source for VisibilityPolicy data? Is it configured in a database table within the Workexec domain, a static configuration file, or managed by a separate Security / People domain service via an API? This defines the critical integration contract.
clarifications_resolved.decision: Security/Policy service is authoritative for permissions and visibility rules; domain services enforce server-side and cache with short TTL + invalidation events.

interpretation.authoritative_source: Security/Policy service is the single source of truth for all visibility policies
interpretation.domain_responsibility: Workexec domain service is responsible for enforcement but NOT policy authorship
interpretation.caching_strategy: Domain services SHALL cache visibility policies with short TTL and event-based invalidation
interpretation.enforcement_location: Server-side enforcement is REQUIRED; client-side filtering is supplementary only
interpretation.integration_contract: API contract SHALL be defined between Security service and domain services

clarifications_resolved.question: The story mentions specific fields (unitPrice, cost, etc.). Is this list exhaustive? Is the policy configurable per-field, or is it a single 'Can View Financials' flag per role? The Acceptance Criteria assume per-field control is desired.
clarifications_resolved.decision: Configurable; use explicit RBAC scopes (domain:resource:action) decoupled from role names.

interpretation.field_level_control: Field-level visibility SHALL be configurable and NOT hardcoded
interpretation.rbac_scope_pattern: RBAC scopes SHALL follow the pattern: domain:resource:action
interpretation.role_decoupling: Role names SHALL be decoupled from permissions (role → permissions mapping)
interpretation.granularity_support: Policy SHALL support granular field-level control, not just coarse-grained flags
interpretation.permission_management: Security service SHALL manage the mapping of roles to permission scopes
interpretation.enforcement_pattern: Domain services SHALL check permission scopes, NOT role names

Added BR-RBAC-2: Role-to-Permission Decoupling
Added AC-RBAC-1: Permission scopes follow domain:resource:action pattern
Added AC-RBAC-2: Code checks permission scopes, NOT role names
Updated VisibilityPolicy entity to include fieldMapping
Updated Functional Behavior to specify permission scope validation
Defined explicit scope pattern in documentation

clarifications_resolved.question: Should this be implemented using a single endpoint that returns a differently shaped DTO based on role, or should we use separate, role-specific endpoints (e.g., /api/workorders/{id}/mechanic-view vs /api/workorders/{id}/full-view)? The functional behavior assumes a single endpoint with a filtered DTO, which is the preferred approach unless otherwise specified.
clarifications_resolved.decision: Use standard best practices with explicit contracts, idempotency, audit trails, UTC timestamps, scoped RBAC, configurable defaults.

interpretation.endpoint_pattern: Use a single endpoint pattern with dynamic DTO filtering based on permissions
interpretation.api_contract: API contract SHALL be explicit and well-documented (OpenAPI/Swagger)
interpretation.idempotency: Idempotency SHALL be implemented for state-changing operations
interpretation.permission_checking: RBAC scopes SHALL be checked on every request (no session-level caching)
interpretation.configurable_defaults: Configurable defaults SHALL be provided for common visibility scenarios
interpretation.error_handling_403: HTTP 403 Forbidden if user lacks minimum required permission scope
interpretation.partial_response: Filtered DTO (omitting fields) if user has partial permissions
